vulnerability.title: Make the auditd Configuration Immutable
vulnerability.description: If the auditd daemon is configured to use the augenrules program to read audit rules during daemon startup (the default), add the following line to a file with suffix .rules in the directory /etc/audit/rules.d in order to make the auditd configuration immutable: -e 2 If the auditd daemon is configured to use the auditctl utility to read audit rules during daemon startup, add the following line to /etc/audit/audit.rules file in order to make the auditd configuration immutable: -e 2 With this setting, a reboot will be required to change any audit rules.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q audit && rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then # Traverse all of: # # /etc/audit/audit.rules, (for auditctl case) # /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules (for augenrules case) # # files to check if '-e .*' setting is present in that '*.rules' file already. # If found, delete such occurrence since auditctl(8) manual page instructs the # '-e 2' rule should be placed as the last rule in the configuration find /etc/audit /etc/audit/rules.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rules' -exec sed -i '/-e[[:space:]]\+.*/d' {} ';' # Append '-e 2' requirement at the end of both: # * /etc/audit/audit.rules file (for auditctl case) # * /etc/audit/rules.d/immutable.rules (for augenrules case) for AUDIT_FILE in "/etc/audit/audit.rules" "/etc/audit/rules.d/i
vulnerability.group: Configure auditd Rules for Comprehensive Auditing

triage_decision.reason: The remediation only adds the '-e 2' rule to the audit configuration, making the auditd rules immutable. This is a standard STIG audit rule change, does not affect authentication, networking, or filesystem layout, and is unlikely to cause lockout or service disruption. The change may require a service restart or later reboot to modify rules, but applying it is safe.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: Requires auditd restart or future reboot to modify rules; Potential loss of ability to change audit rules without reboot

reasoning_messages.reasoning:
We need to remediate audit_rules_immutable: add "-e 2" as last rule in appropriate file(s). Need to determine whether audit daemon uses augenrules (default) or auditctl. Usually Rocky Linux uses augenrules, reading from /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules and compiled to /etc/audit/audit.rules at startup. So we should add "-e 2" as a file with suffix .rules in /etc/audit/rules.d (maybe a dedicated file). The description says add line to a file with suffix .rules in directory /etc/audit/rules.d. Could create a new file like /etc/audit/rules.d/99-immutable.rules containing "-e 2". Or add to existing .rules files. Safer to create new file.

Steps:
1. Use read_file to list files in /etc/audit/rules.d maybe via run_cmd 'ls /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules'. But reading directory via run_cmd. Could just check existence of a file that contains '-e '. Use grep. But we need to inspect before modify.

Plan:
- Use run_cmd "ls /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules" to get list. If none, fallback to /etc/audit/audit.rules.
- For each file, read it to check for '-e' line. We'll use run_cmd to grep. But we must read files individually with read_file.

Simplify: create a new file /etc/audit/rules.d/99-immutable.rules with content "-e 2". Ensure not duplicate. Check if any existing .rules file already contains '-e' line. Use run_cmd "grep -R \"^-e\" /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules" . If result non-empty, we should not add duplicate. But we can still add in new file; duplicate may cause warning but rule expects only one -e 2 line. Safer to remove any existing -e lines from all .rules files then add our file.

We can run sed -i '/^-e[[:space:]]\+.*/d' on each file. Use run_cmd for each file.

Thus plan:
- Get list of .rules files via run_cmd.
- For each, run_cmd "sed -i '/^-e[[:space:]]\\+.*/d' <file>"
- Then write new file /etc/audit/rules.d/99-immutable.rules with content "-e 2\n"
- Then restart auditd service: run_cmd "systemctl restart auditd"

Make sure to read a file before modifying: we can read first file to see content.

We'll propose this plan.

review_feedback: The plan adds the required '-e 2' rule but only creates it in /etc/audit/rules.d/99-immutable.rules. On systems that use auditctl (reading /etc/audit/audit.rules) this file will be ignored, so the immutability setting would not be applied. The remediation should also ensure the rule is present in /etc/audit/audit.rules when that is the active configuration, and that it is the last rule in the file. Until that is added, the plan may not fully resolve the vulnerability.

concerns: Does not handle the auditctl case where /etc/audit/audit.rules is used.
Assumes a simple restart of auditd will apply the new rule; some implementations require a reboot after setting '-e 2'.
Potential for duplicate '-e' lines if other scripts add the rule elsewhere.
suggested_improvements: Detect whether the system is using augenrules or auditctl (e.g., check /etc/audit/auditd.conf for 'auditctl' or 'augenrules').
If auditctl is in use, append '-e 2' to /etc/audit/audit.rules after removing any existing '-e' lines.
Ensure the '-e 2' line is the very last line in the file(s) being used.
Document that a reboot may be required to modify rules after immutability is set.
